models.name: Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M
models.description: IBM/NASA Prithvi Earth Observation 2.0 foundation model (300M parameters). Pre-trained on Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) multi-band satellite imagery for general-purpose geospatial feature extraction and downstream Earth observation tasks.
models.input_description: Multi-band satellite imagery (HLS), 6 spectral bands, 224x224 pixel patches
known_limitations: Requires 224x224 input patches — larger images must be tiled
Pre-trained on HLS data only — performance may degrade on other sensor types
Requires fine-tuning for specific downstream tasks
models.notes: Base foundation model. Use task-specific fine-tuned variants (floods, burn scars) for production applications.

models.name: Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M-TL-Sen1Floods11
models.description: Fine-tuned variant of Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M for flood mapping using Sentinel-1/2 imagery. Transfer-learned on the Sen1Floods11 benchmark dataset for binary flood segmentation.
models.input_description: Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery
known_limitations: Trained on Sen1Floods11 — may not generalize to all flood scenarios
Binary segmentation only (flood vs. non-flood)
Performance depends on cloud-free imagery availability
models.notes: Use this model specifically for flood mapping tasks. Do not use the base Prithvi model for flood detection without fine-tuning.

models.name: Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M-BurnScars
models.description: Fine-tuned variant of Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M for burn scar detection from satellite imagery. Identifies post-wildfire burned areas through semantic segmentation.
models.input_description: Multi-band satellite imagery (HLS) with shortwave infrared bands
known_limitations: Detects post-fire burn scars only — not active fire detection
Requires cloud-free post-fire imagery
May confuse burn scars with dark soil or shadows in some terrain
models.notes: Designed for post-wildfire damage assessment. For active fire detection, use thermal band analysis algorithms instead.

models.name: Microsoft Aurora
models.description: Microsoft Aurora foundation model for weather and climate prediction. Large-scale atmospheric model capable of high-resolution weather forecasting using AI, trained on ERA5 reanalysis and other atmospheric datasets.
models.input_description: Atmospheric state variables (temperature, pressure, humidity, wind) on pressure levels, surface variables
known_limitations: Large model requiring significant GPU memory (8+ GB)
Forecast skill degrades beyond 10-day lead times
May not capture sub-grid-scale phenomena accurately
Requires ERA5-compatible input formatting
models.notes: Large model, requires significant GPU memory. Use for weather forecasting tasks only — do not confuse with Aurora Wave for ocean applications.

models.name: Aurora Wave
models.description: Aurora Wave model for ocean wave forecasting. Specialized variant of the Aurora framework designed for predicting ocean wave conditions including significant wave height, period, and direction.
models.input_description: Ocean surface state variables, wind fields, wave spectra
known_limitations: Specialized for wave forecasting — not a general ocean model
Performance may vary in coastal and shallow water regions
Requires wind forcing fields as input
models.notes: Different application from base Aurora — do not interchange. Use this for ocean wave tasks and base Aurora for atmospheric tasks.

models.name: Prithvi Weather-Climate (WxC)
models.description: NASA/IBM Prithvi Weather-Climate foundation model. A large-scale AI model for weather and climate applications, pre-trained on MERRA-2 reanalysis data for downstream weather prediction and climate analysis tasks.
models.input_description: Atmospheric state variables from reanalysis (MERRA-2 format), multi-level pressure and surface fields
known_limitations: Pre-trained on MERRA-2 — may not generalize to other reanalysis formats without adaptation
Requires fine-tuning for specific downstream tasks
Computationally expensive for full-resolution inference
models.notes: NASA/IBM collaborative foundation model. Complementary to Microsoft Aurora — Prithvi-WxC focuses on longer-range climate applications.

models.name: SeisBench
models.description: SeisBench is a comprehensive seismological machine learning benchmark framework providing standardized interfaces for seismic data, pre-trained models (PhaseNet, EQTransformer, etc.), and benchmark datasets for earthquake detection and phase picking.
models.input_description: Seismic waveform data in standard formats (MiniSEED, SAC) via ObsPy
known_limitations: Framework — not a model itself; provides access to multiple models
Model performance varies by region and network configuration
Requires ObsPy for seismic data handling
models.notes: Meta-framework for seismological ML. Use specific models (PhaseNet, EQTransformer) through this interface.

models.name: PhaseNet
models.description: PhaseNet is a deep neural network for seismic phase picking. It identifies P-wave and S-wave arrival times in continuous seismic waveforms with high precision, accessible through the SeisBench framework.
models.input_description: Three-component (ZNE or Z12) seismic waveform data, typically 30-second windows at 100 Hz
known_limitations: Optimized for local/regional earthquakes — may miss teleseismic phases
Performance depends on signal-to-noise ratio
Trained primarily on broadband station data
models.notes: Accessed through SeisBench framework. One of the most widely used seismic phase pickers in modern seismology.

models.name: EQTransformer
models.description: EQTransformer is a multi-task deep learning model for simultaneous earthquake detection, P-wave picking, and S-wave picking. Uses attention mechanisms to process continuous seismic waveforms, accessible through SeisBench.
models.input_description: Three-component seismic waveform data, 60-second windows at 100 Hz
known_limitations: May produce false positives in high-noise environments
Trained on STEAD dataset — performance varies by region
Slower inference than PhaseNet due to attention layers
models.notes: Multi-task model providing both detection and picking. Use PhaseNet for phase picking only; use EQTransformer when both detection and picking are needed.

models.name: Surya Solar Foundation Model
models.description: NASA/IBM Surya is a foundation model for solar physics and heliophysics. Pre-trained on Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) imagery across multiple wavelengths for solar feature recognition and space weather applications.
models.input_description: Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) AIA and HMI imagery across multiple EUV/UV wavelengths
known_limitations: Pre-trained on SDO data — may not generalize to other solar observatories without adaptation
Requires fine-tuning for specific downstream tasks
Solar imagery preprocessing (limb correction, normalization) required
models.notes: Foundation model for heliophysics. Requires SDO-format input imagery. Fine-tune for specific tasks like flare prediction or coronal hole detection.

models.name: NASA/IBM Lunar Foundation Model — Crater Detection
models.description: Fine-tuned crater detection model from the NASA/IBM Lunar Foundation Model. Identifies and segments impact craters on the lunar surface from orbital imagery.
models.input_description: Lunar orbital imagery (e.g., LROC NAC/WAC), grayscale or multi-band
known_limitations: Trained on lunar imagery ONLY — do NOT use for Mars crater detection
Performance varies with illumination angle and image resolution
May miss heavily degraded or overlapping craters
Not validated for other planetary bodies
models.notes: Trained on lunar imagery ONLY. Do NOT use for Mars crater detection. A separate Mars-specific model would be required for Martian crater analysis.

models.name: Zoobot ConvNeXt-Nano
models.description: Zoobot galaxy morphology classifier using a ConvNeXt-Nano backbone. Pre-trained on Galaxy Zoo volunteer classifications for automated galaxy morphological analysis including spiral arm detection, bar identification, and merger classification.
models.input_description: Galaxy cutout images (RGB or single-band), typically 224x224 pixels from survey imaging
known_limitations: Trained on Galaxy Zoo data — biased toward bright, resolved galaxies
Classification scheme follows Galaxy Zoo decision tree
May not generalize to very high-redshift or faint galaxies
Nano variant trades accuracy for speed — use larger variants for research-grade results
models.notes: Lightweight variant suitable for rapid morphological screening. For detailed research, consider larger Zoobot variants.

models.name: AstroCLIP
models.description: AstroCLIP is a multi-modal astronomy foundation model from the Polymathic AI initiative. It aligns galaxy images and spectra in a shared embedding space using contrastive learning, enabling cross-modal retrieval and zero-shot classification.
models.input_description: Galaxy images (multi-band survey cutouts) or optical spectra (flux vs. wavelength arrays)
known_limitations: Expensive model — high GPU memory requirement
Trained on DESI Legacy Survey data — may not generalize to all surveys
Cross-modal alignment may degrade for rare or unusual objects
Requires specific input preprocessing pipeline
models.notes: Optional — expensive model, only load if explicitly requested. Powerful for cross-modal astronomy tasks but resource-intensive.
